entries.notes: Theorem B.1 (l.819) against EGF.universality_of_ergodic, hypothesis by hypothesis. 'a measured space with lambda finite' is any MeasurableSpace S with [IsFiniteMeasure lam]; finiteness is also v2's standing assumption (l.161). 'pi* a Markov kernel on S' is [IsMarkovKernel pi]. 'admits a finite invariant measure lambda-hat equivalent to lambda' is [IsFiniteMeasure lamHat], hinv : lamHat.bind pi = lamHat, hac : lamHat << lam and hac' : lam << lamHat. 'for which it is ergodic' is herg : IsKernelErgodic pi lamHat. 'any probability distributions F_init, F_term << lambda' is [IsProbabilityMeasure Finit], [IsProbabilityMeasure Fterm], hinit and hterm. 'any eps > 0' is hε. The conclusion 'a bounded f_out >= 0 such that (pi*, f_out) from F_init to F_term has delta F_init(S) + delta F_term(S) < eps' is the Lean's, minus MemLp fout 2 lam, which bounded on a finite lambda implies. The outflow is lam.withDensity (ofReal fout). initialError and terminalError are (F_term + F_out - F_init - F_in)^+ and (F_init + F_in - F_term - F_out)^+, i.e. v2's delta F_init and delta F_term (l.329). The converse: 'if pi* is not ergodic for lambda-hat, some such pair has delta F_init(S) + delta F_term(S) >= 2 for every f_out'. That is EGF.not_universal_of_not_ergodic (hypothesis: not IsKernelErgodic pi lam, for lambda, with lambda finite and pi Markov), moved from lambda to lambda-hat by EGF.isKernelErgodic_congr (lambda-hat ~ lambda). 'Such pair' means probability distributions << lambda. The Lean also gives bounded densities, so the TeX claims less. 'For every f_out' ranges over outflows of generative flows, which are finite (l.161), so the Lean's IsFiniteMeasure Fout, Fout << lam covers it. EGF.universal_iff_ergodic packages both directions. Theorem 3.4 (l.288) is EGF.universality_of_ergodic_family: lambda finite (standing), pi with a finite invariant lambda-hat ~ lambda and ergodic for it, D (the f_out with (pi*, f_out) in the family) with IsDenseNonnegConeL2 lam D, conclusion IsUniversalFamilyEps (Definition 3.2 as fixed by C-18/C-19). 'Family of EGF' is narrower than the Lean's arbitrary family, which is harmless. The sentence at l.821: 'universality itself needs only ergodicity' is B.1. 'When lambda itself is invariant, summable L2-mixing gives the outflow as a convergent series (see the remark)' is a pointer to C-21's remark and inherits its scope (finding 1). Section 6: l.732 'which universality does not need (Theorem B.1)' and l.738 'not needed for universality' are true in both readings. B.1 assumes no mixing, and universal non-mixing witnesses exist (EGF.Swap.universal_not_summablyMixing, EGF.universal_not_summablyMixing_addCircle). added_hypotheses: 'the invariant measure equivalent to lambda is finite' is in B.1 and in Theorem 3.4. 'lambda finite' is v2's standing assumption made explicit, not an addition. The Polish structure, the L2 densities and the mixing are dropped, so the edit adds no hypothesis the entry does not list. The kind is strengthening, with no refutation. The applied texts are C-29's `corrected` verbatim (checked by whitespace-normalized comparison), with two differences. 'Definition 3.3' is written Definition~ref{def:summably_mixing}, which renders 'Definition 3.3', for a label added at l.272. The emph around the statement is dropped: the theorem environment is theoremstyle plain (l.43), so the body is already italic, and emph would have set it upright. That choice is right. The paragraph that introduces Theorem 3.4 (l.271, l.282) and the Discussion's reference to B.1's proof (l.699) are left inconsistent (findings 2 and 3).

The proof (l.824-830) is C-39's `corrected` verbatim and says only what the anchors prove, step by step. eta = eps/5, norms being total variation norms (EGF.tvMass, the full |mu - nu|(S), not the halved TV of Section 3.2). Truncation: EGF.exists_truncation (needs lam << lamHat) gives probability densities a, b <= K and <= K d(lambda-hat)/d(lambda), with tvMass < eta. 'every mu_j pi^t <= K lambda-hat' follows from pushIter_mono and invariance. 'P is a contraction of L2(lambda-hat)' is Markov.norm_densityActionL2_le (lambda-hat finite invariant). 'Whose fixed points are constant' is EGF.Markov.ae_eq_const_of_densityAction_eq (integrable fixed points are a.e. constant under IsKernelErgodic pi lamHat). von Neumann: EGF.Markov.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_densityActionL2, for the mean-zero h (|h| <= K, so h is in L2). 'Some N >= 1 has ||sum_{t<N} (mu_0 - mu_1) pi^t|| < N eta' is EGF.exists_tvMass_cesaro_lt_of_ergodic. R = N K lambda-hat is invariant and dominates the partial sums for T < N (hsumle in universality_of_ergodic). F is (1/N) EGF.cesaroOutflow, >= 0. The telescoping is EGF.tvMass_construction_cesaro. The TeX writes it as an identity of signed measures, which holds because R >= B_T. The Lean proves the cancellation-free form (hX, hY) and states the resulting inequality of norms. 'The kernel being a contraction for TV' is tvMass_bind_le. Truncating F's density at M gives a bounded f_out. The '5 eta' counts five triangle terms: F_init vs mu_0, F_M pi vs F pi, the Cesaro defect, F vs F_M, mu_1 vs F_term (e1-e5 in the Lean proof). The paper does not list them, and it does not need to. Necessity: 'pi*(x,A) = 1_A(x) for lambda-hat-a.e. x and 0 < lambda(A) < lambda(S)' is the negation of IsKernelErgodic (null sets of lambda and lambda-hat agree). The Lean takes lambda-a.e. Then (F_out pi)(A) = F_out(A) for every finite F_out << lambda (hbind of EGF.two_le_errors_of_invariant_set), so the defect has mass 1 on A and -1 on A^c, and the errors sum to >= 2. Corrector's choices. (2) The pi*(x,A) notation is standard and unambiguous. It differs from l.157's P(pi(x) in A) and Appendix A's pi*(s -> Y), which is cosmetic (finding 8). (3) The counter step is verified: a v1 build numbers the printed proof (40)-(45) and Appendix C (46)-(51). The working-copy build numbers (39), then (46)-(51) in Appendix C, the same equations (TV bound, flow-matching chain, f~_term). No label number changes (aux diff: only def:summably_mixing 3.3 is new). The cost is a visible gap (39) -> (46), which is the author's call (finding 8). Kind gap, no refutation, added_hypotheses [] is right.

The remark (l.834) is C-21's `corrected` verbatim. Clause by clause. 'If lambda itself is invariant ... summably L2-mixing with lambda-hat = lambda' is the listed added hypothesis, present. 'The coefficients are then submultiplicative' is EGF.mixingCoeff_self_add_le (lambda finite, hinv). 'Sum gamma_n < infinity gives gamma_N < 1 for some N' is EGF.tsum_mixingCoeff_self_ne_top_iff. 'gamma_n <= C rho^n' is EGF.hasExponentialL2Decay_iff / hasExponentialL2Decay_of_mixingCoeff_lt_one. 'The Cesaro weights can be dropped': EGF.tvMass_construction, the plain truncated Neumann outflow, against tvMass_construction_cesaro. 'The series converges absolutely in L2(lambda)' for L2 densities is not a declaration. It is a one-line consequence of the decay (||phi pi^t||_2^2 <= gamma_t ||phi||_2^2 by homogeneity of the transfer, then a geometric series), acceptable in a remark. 'Its partial sums, lifted by a multiple of lambda, give the outflow directly' is FALSE for densities in L2(lambda) that are unbounded. That case is the one the remark names (finding 1). The anchor EGF.tvMass_construction needs hB: sum_{t<=T} mu_1 pi^t <= R. With R = c lambda this forces d F_term/d lambda <= c a.e., so it fits only a bounded F_term density. v1 took the positive part of the lifted limit, which the remark does not. The refuting instance is the resampling kernel, EGF.isSummablyL2Mixing_const and EGF.pushIter_const_succ. The failure of non-negativity itself is elementary and not in Lean. The clause is true and anchored for bounded densities: R = (T+1) K lambda is invariant and dominates sum_{t<=T} mu_1 pi^t, and the defect is <= ||(mu_0 - mu_1) pi^{T+1}||_TV -> 0 (EGF.exists_tvMass_pushIter_lt_of_tendsto at lambda-hat = lambda, which also takes both densities bounded). The outflow's density is then bounded, as B.1 asks. added_hypotheses lists 'lambda invariant (lambda-hat = lambda)' and it is in the remark. The edit adds no unlisted hypothesis, but the corrected form needs one, bounded densities, to be listed after the fix. Kind gap, no refutation. The marker l.835 is fine. Typeset as an unnumbered textit{Remark.}: the remark environment is numbered within the theorem counter and would have renumbered the Appendix B theorems (theo:spectral_gap_tori, ...). The unnumbered form keeps them, so the choice is right.

l.284 against the anchors. 'Satisfied if lambda is invariant, lambda pi = lambda, and the Koopman operator phi -> d((phi lambda) pi)/d lambda has spectral radius < 1 on {int phi d lambda = 0}' is EGF.isSummablyL2Mixing_of_mixingCoeff_lt_one / isSummablyL2Mixing_of_pow_contraction: lambda finite (standing), pi Markov, hinv, and gamma_N < 1 for some N, which gives IsSummablyL2Mixing pi lambda with lambda-hat = lambda. gamma_N is ||T^N||^2 on the mean-zero subspace by definition (EGF.mixingCoeff with transfer). The step from 'spectral radius < 1' to 'there is N with ||T^N|| < 1' is Gelfand's formula. It is classical, not formalized, and disclosed in the SCOPE of EGF/MixingCriteria.lean. T preserves the mean (integral_transfer) and contracts L2(lambda) under invariance (eLpNorm_transfer_le), so 'spectral radius on the subspace' is well posed. '(For a reversible pi: its spectrum there lies in [-1+c, 1-c])' is EGF.isSummablyL2Mixing_of_reversible with IsReversibleL2 and HasTwoSidedSpectralGap. For a self-adjoint T, the Rayleigh form |<T phi, phi>| <= (1-c)||phi||^2 is the spectral inclusion, and for such T spectral radius < 1 is that inclusion. 'A spectrum bounded away from 1 only is not enough (the swap of two points)' is EGF.Swap.transfer_eq_neg, EGF.Swap.not_isSummablyL2Mixing, EGF.not_spectralGapRemarkPrinted. 'In this case, the convergence of iterates by pi is exponential' is HasExponentialL2Decay (EGF.hasExponentialL2Decay_of_mixingCoeff_lt_one, EGF.hasExponentialL2Decay_iff). Refutations answered. The swap (lambda uniform and invariant, spectrum {-1} on mean-zero functions) has spectral radius 1 and is excluded. The Sink of EGF.not_spectralRadiusCriterionWithoutInvariance (lambda not invariant) is excluded by lambda pi = lambda. EGF.not_spectralGapRemarkExponentialPrinted is excluded likewise. Both added_hypotheses (lambda invariant; spectral radius < 1, two-sided for reversible) are in the text and no other is added. Corrector's choice 1. lambda pi = lambda for the register's lambda pi* = lambda is right: Definition 3.3 and the whole sentence use the plain pi, and the register's form would mix the two. Keeping cite{conze2013ergodicity} departs from `corrected`, which drops it. It is v2's only citation of that entry: dropping it would remove the entry from main.bbl, which is tracked because arXiv builds without BibTeX, and the corrector may write main.tex only. It now sits right after the corrected criterion, unchecked (finding 4).

findings.where: main.tex:834 (C-21's remark); main.tex:821 (C-29's pointer to it)
findings.what: Overclaim. 'For F_init, F_term with densities in L2(lambda) the series ... converges absolutely in L2(lambda), and its partial sums, lifted by a multiple of lambda, give the outflow directly.' The second clause is false for unbounded L2 densities. Counterexample: S = [0,1], lambda Lebesgue, pi(x, .) = lambda, the resampling kernel. It is invariant and summably L2-mixing with lambda-hat = lambda, since gamma_n = 0 for n >= 1 (EGF.isSummablyL2Mixing_const, EGF.pushIter_const_succ). Take F_init = lambda and F_term = (3/4) x^{-1/4} lambda (a probability, with density in L2: int (9/16) x^{-1/2} = 9/8). For t >= 1, (F_init - F_term) pi^t = 0, so every partial sum is F_init - F_term, whose density 1 - (3/4) x^{-1/4} is unbounded below. No partial sum plus c lambda is a non-negative measure, let alone a bounded outflow. The anchor EGF.tvMass_construction needs hB: sum_{t<=T} mu_1 pi^t <= R. With R = c lambda that forces a bounded F_term density, as the corrector noted. v1 used the positive part of the lifted limit; the remark drops that step and says 'directly'. With bounded densities (<= K) the clause is true and anchored. R = (T+1) K lambda is invariant (lambda pi = lambda) and dominates the partial sums of mu_1. The defect is <= ||(F_init - F_term) pi^{T+1}||_TV, which tends to 0 (EGF.exists_tvMass_pushIter_lt_of_tendsto at lambda-hat = lambda, which also takes both densities bounded). The outflow's density is then bounded, as B.1 states. The L2 convergence is a one-line consequence of gamma_t <= C rho^t, not a declaration. l.821 ('summable L2-mixing gives the outflow as a convergent series (see the remark after the proof)') follows B.1, which covers every F << lambda, so it inherits the remark's scope.
findings.fix: C-21 round 2. Smallest wording: at l.834 replace 'with densities in $L^2(\lambda)$' by 'with bounded densities'. Both clauses then hold, the convergence because bounded densities are in L2 on a finite lambda. Optionally append ' (for general $\Finit,\Fterm\ll\lambda$, after truncating their densities as in the proof)'. That makes l.821's pointer exact for B.1's setting, through EGF.exists_truncation and the route of EGF.main_universality_of_tendsto. A stronger alternative: '... with densities in $L^2(\lambda)$ the series ... then converges absolutely in $L^2(\lambda)$; for bounded densities its partial sums, lifted by a multiple of $\lambda$, give the outflow directly.' Register: C-21 added_hypotheses += 'bounded densities, for the lift (with unbounded L2 densities no multiple of lambda makes the partial sums non-negative)'. anchor += EGF.isSummablyL2Mixing_const (the boundary instance), plus EGF.exists_truncation if the parenthetical is taken. Update `corrected` to the new text.

findings.what: A reference to the replaced proof. 'Lastly, from the proof of the universality Theorem ref{theo:universality}, we observe that f_out* can be obtained as a fixed point of a flow operator dependent on pi*, F_init, and F_term. This operator is a contraction for the affine toroidal family.' (v1 l.664, unchanged, in no entry.) After C-39, the proof (that of B.1, since Theorem 3.4 has none) builds f_out from a Cesaro-weighted Neumann sum and a truncation. It has no fixed point. Only C-21's remark (lambda invariant, summable mixing) yields a series whose L2 sum nu_infty satisfies nu_infty = nu_infty pi + F_init - F_term, and the outflow comes from its lifted partial sums, not from the fixed point (finding 1). 'A contraction for the affine toroidal family' is unproved. A power of the operator is a contraction when gamma_N < 1. C-28 mentions a norm < 1 for the minimal four moves at b = 0 via Kesten (not formalized), and for trained alpha lambda need not even be invariant. CHECK-1 and CHECK-2 of T-egf-correct-universality predicted this inconsistency once C-39 landed.
findings.fix: A new `found` entry (printed main.tex:664), for this batch's round 2 since C-39 causes it, or as C-39 round 2 extending its `printed`. Proposed text: 'Lastly, when $\lambda$ is invariant and $\ForwardPolicyStar$ summably $L^2$-mixing (the remark after the proof of Theorem~\ref{theo:universality_true}), $\foutstar$ can be obtained from the partial sums of a series whose sum is a fixed point of the flow operator $\nu\mapsto\nu\ForwardPolicyStar+\Finit-\Fterm$, some power of which is a contraction.' Drop 'This operator is a contraction for the affine toroidal family' unless proved. Candidate anchors: EGF.tsum_mixingCoeff_self_ne_top_iff (gamma_N < 1, i.e. ||T^N|| < 1 on mean-zero functions) and EGF.tvMass_construction. The fixed-point identity of the L2 sum is elementary and not in Lean.

findings.what: Section 6's first paragraph is consistent but has lost its point. 'Although ergodicity is easily achievable ..., the technical assumption of L2-mixing summability, which universality does not need (Theorem B.1), is more subtle. EGFs suffer from limited proven applicability, further theory is needed to easily enforce L2-mixing summability ...' The contrast was built on 'needed for universality'. Now the text says neither what mixing buys (the convergent series of C-21, and perhaps training) nor why its subtlety limits applicability. The last sentence, 'two transformations are sufficient to achieve universality', is true but not minimal: one ergodic affine map suffices on T^d, d >= 2 (EGF.exists_universality_tori_single_move), and a.e. translation on any torus (EGF.ae_universality_tori_translation). It also disagrees with the 'four' of l.149, l.306 and l.321, as in v1. Nothing here is false.

'There is extensive mathematical literature on the so-called spectral gap [kontoyiannis2012geometric, guivarc2016spectral, marrakchi2018strongly, bekka2020spectral], which is a sufficient condition for L2-mixing summability.' C-29's edit of the first sentence is fine.

answers.choice_4_C21_precision: The clause is NOT true as applied. With unbounded L2 densities (resampling kernel, F_init = lambda, F_term = (3/4) x^{-1/4} lambda on [0,1]) every partial sum is F_init - F_term, unbounded below, so no multiple of lambda makes it an outflow. EGF.tvMass_construction fits only when R = c lambda dominates sum_{t<=T} F_term pi^t, i.e. for a bounded F_term density. The smallest true and anchored wording replaces 'with densities in $L^2(\lambda)$' by 'with bounded densities', optionally adding '(for general F_init, F_term << lambda, after truncating their densities as in the proof)'. The register then adds 'bounded densities' to C-21's added_hypotheses (finding 1).
